resources.string: Add a proxy in the Proxies tab, then create rules to choose which traffic uses it.
Rules apply to every app that is in the tunnel. Android does not say which app made a connection, so rules match the destination. Choose the apps below.
Traffic is sent only to the proxies you add. ProxyBridge collects no data and has no analytics.
Rules are checked from top to bottom. Hold and drag to reorder, swipe to delete.
The first proxy is the default one, used by rules that do not name a proxy. Hold and drag to reorder, swipe to delete.
On: the proxy gets the site\'s name when the device looked it up through the system DNS, and the IP address otherwise. Off: the proxy always gets the IP address.
Optional. Leave the user name empty if the proxy needs no login.
Enter a host and a port from 1 to 65535.

Domains, IP addresses or CIDR blocks separated by semicolons. Leave empty to match any host. A domain only matches when the app looked it up through the system DNS, so apps with their own encrypted DNS are matched by IP only.
Leave the ports empty to match any port.
An HTTP proxy cannot carry UDP. UDP traffic matched by this rule goes direct.
Only the apps in the tunnel are affected by ProxyBridge. Other apps connect as usual.
ProxyBridge sends the network traffic of this device through the SOCKS5 or HTTP proxies you add, using an Android VPN connection. Android asks you to allow it the first time you turn it on.

Traffic you send through a proxy goes to that proxy, and whoever runs it can see it. Traffic you send direct goes straight to its destination. None of it is sent to us. Name lookups go to the DNS servers of your network, or to public ones if none can be found.
None. ProxyBridge has no account, no analytics, no advertising and no tracking. Your proxies, passwords and rules stay on this device.
We do not sell, use or disclose any data to third parties.
To match rules written for a domain, ProxyBridge reads the names in this device\'s DNS lookups while it is on. They are kept in memory only and are never stored or sent anywhere.
